0.long_answer: Glycogen storage disease type XV (GSD XV) is a metabolic disorder that results from a deficiency of the enzyme glycogenin-1, which is encoded by the GYG1 gene. This gene is located on the long arm of chromosome 3. The enzyme glycogenin-1 plays a crucial role in initiating glycogen synthesis by undergoing autoglycosylation. A deficiency in this enzyme disrupts the normal process of glycogen formation, leading to abnormal glycogen accumulation and muscle weakness, among other symptoms. The disease is therefore classified as glycogen storage disease type XV.
